Date: October 23, 2026
Verdict: READY — MANUAL SAVE REQUIRED
Status: Native save route reviewed; no save or reload performed. The existing Editor remains running.

3. Native Editor save mechanism analysis

This analysis uses the installed official UE 5.6 source files, not an assumption based on the ForgeMCP adapter's function name. Numbered excerpts and source-file SHA-256 hashes are preserved in native_save_source_evidence.txt [not indexed]

Verified command chain:

  1. LevelEditorMenu.cpp:45-71 registers the Save command in LevelEditor.MainMenu.File.
  2. LevelEditorActions.cpp:4071 labels it Save Current Level, default shortcut Ctrl+S.
  3. LevelEditor.cpp:679 binds that command to FLevelEditorActionCallbacks::Save.
  4. LevelEditorActions.cpp:464-476 routes an existing non-temporary world directly to FEditorFileUtils::SaveCurrentLevel. The temporary-world Save As branch does not apply here.
  5. FileHelpers.cpp:4151-4198 implements SaveCurrentLevel. It inspects the current level package and loaded external-object packages. It adds the map only if dirty/new. It adds external packages if dirty/new/empty. It guards bSkipExternalObjectSave=true before calling InternalSavePackages, using bPromptUserToSave=false, bFastSave=false and bCheckDirty=false because selection was already performed.
  6. FileHelpers.cpp:3903 onward routes the selected list through PromptForCheckoutAndSave and InternalPromptForCheckoutAndSave, preserving a bounded package list rather than enumerating all dirty project assets.
  7. FileHelpers.cpp:3428 onward resolves an existing package to its existing filename. For these existing non-map external actor packages, it invokes SaveAsset. FileHelpers.cpp:1054 onward saves the same named package; the external-save helper respects the skip guard for packages that are not newly created.

Consequences for the verified current state:

  • The Landscape root and all 16 dirty streaming-proxy external packages are selected.
  • The clean, existing map is omitted. A dirty/new map would change scope; this readiness assessment would then be invalid.
  • Clean other external actor packages are omitted. Dirty unrelated assets not owned by this level are not enumerated by this command.
  • The two /Script packages are outside the selected level/external package set.
  • All reviewed packages already exist and are not newly created. No Save As, duplication, rename, component replacement or World Partition reconfiguration is needed. Existing World Partition package identities and filenames are preserved by the selected path.
  • FileHelpers.cpp:4254 can delete empty packages during ordinary save handling. The fresh preview confirms no empty external actor package is scheduled for deletion; will_delete=false throughout. If the scene changes before saving, this guarantee must be rechecked.

Automatic-restoration assessment:

The ordinary Editor command invokes the engine saving route directly. It does not enter FForgeLevels::Handle(current_level_save_apply) and therefore does not execute ForgeLevels.cpp:651-665, the adapter-specific copy-back/delete recovery loop that blocked Stage 2B. The inspected ordinary per-package failure path reports Cancel/Retry/Continue and can leave partial saves; it does not restore the verified ForgeMCP checkpoint over production. No checkpoint-recovery wrapper is invoked by this manual command.

A separate source-control caveat was investigated: FileHelpers.cpp:245 enables an alternate checkout workflow only for a provider named Unreal Revision Control with automatic checkout enabled; that path can later invoke RevertAndReloadPackages (line 4740). The current Editor session log reports revision control disabled, with no subsequent enable/provider-change evidence. Standard checkout paths also contain special handling for source-control-deleted files; the intended files exist, are writable and are not pending empty-package deletion in the reviewed state. Do not enable/change revision control for this save. If an unexpected checkout/revert/reload prompt appears, cancel and report it rather than authorizing any revert.

The conclusion is specific to the current verified existing-package/offline source-control state. It is not a claim that every Editor save path under every provider lacks reversion behavior. Normal native temporary-file/write handling is distinct from restoring a recovery checkpoint; a low-level save failure still requires post-save inspection.

No plugin modification, source edit, rebuild, new grant or Editor restart is required for this manual command.

  • will_save=true: exactly 17.
  • will_delete=true: zero.
  • Clean map will_save=false.
  • Five unrelated external actor packages will_save=false.
  • Every selected production package resolves to the Landscape root or one of its 16 native proxy descriptors.
  • Selected set exactly matches the historical preview and current dirty production inventory.

No apply preview will be invoked, and the user does not need either preview ID for the native menu command. Preview expiry has no effect on the existing layer state.

The inspected SaveCurrentLevel selection conditions match the conditions used by the preview's native GatherCurrentSavePackages helper. The preview supplies current nonempty/existing package evidence; source tracing establishes the ordinary menu route independently.

5. Whether a safe manual-save route was established

Yes — READY — MANUAL SAVE REQUIRED, for the unchanged reviewed state.

Exact supported interaction for the user:

  1. Keep the existing ForgeMCPDev Editor open with L_City_World_Master as the active persistent level and PIE stopped. Do not edit actors, layers, packages, configuration or revision-control state before this save.
  2. In the main Level Editor, choose File → Save Current Level once. The default Ctrl+S binding while the Level Editor is focused maps to the same command, but the explicit File-menu entry avoids invoking an asset editor's Save command.
  3. Allow the operation to finish, then report completion here so Codex can perform read-only verification. Leave the Editor and level open.

The expected write scope is exactly the 17 existing Landscape external actor packages listed above. No map write, package deletion, unrelated asset save or ForgeMCP automatic restore is expected in the reviewed state.

If any dialog requests Save As, Revert, Reload, or includes unexpected package scope, cancel and report it. If any package fails, choose Cancel to stop further saving; do not choose Retry/Continue, repeat the command or attempt recovery. Some packages may already have saved; preserve that resulting state for read-only review.

The user must perform this operation personally. Codex has neither simulated interaction nor invoked a save command. This report is a concrete review of the route, not a claim of completed persistence.

6. User save confirmation, if performed

Pending. The user has not yet reported performing this Stage 2C manual save. No save execution is attributed to Codex or the user in this report.

After confirmation, obtain fresh native dirty inventory and file hashes. A user statement alone is not proof that all packages saved.

7. Files saved and their new hashes

None yet verified as saved. No save or restore was invoked during this Stage 2C preparation. The pre-save hashes for all 17 targets are recorded above, and the broader 1,530-file Content baseline is retained for the next read-only verification.

After the manual save, compare exact Content membership and hashes, require the 17 production dirty flags to clear, record every new target SHA-256, inspect save logs, and identify any unauthorized changed/added/deleted file. Do not automatically retry or restore a partial result.

9. Reload verification, if safely available

No reload has been performed. The Editor remains running with the unsaved adopted state intact. No opening of an already-loaded level is counted as persistence proof.

Only after a verified save may a supported disk reread be reviewed. It must preserve unrelated work, discard no relevant unsaved packages and actually reload saved production packages. The consumed adoption grant is not reused. No forced reload or restart is permitted.

If those conditions cannot be established after saving, the correct outcome is SAVED — RELOAD VERIFICATION PENDING. This report cannot yet use that verdict because the manual save has not been verified.

10. Remaining risks

  • Readiness is a point-in-time scope assessment. Any new dirty/deleted/new package, active-world change, source-control change or terrain edit requires revalidation.
  • Native save is not an atomic 17-package transaction. Failure/cancellation can leave a partial save, and the normal path's boolean result is not sufficient proof of every package outcome. Native dirty flags, exact file hashes, logs and integrity readback must be checked afterward.
  • Normal engine save delegates and source-control bookkeeping can run. The read-only scope audit establishes the selected asset package set; the post-save file audit is still required to detect unexpected side effects.
  • The session log records disabled revision control; the exposed ForgeMCP tools do not provide a dedicated live revision-control provider query. Do not enable it or accept checkout/revert actions. An unexpected provider prompt invalidates this reviewed route.
  • Config/DefaultEditorPerProjectUserSettings.ini retains its previously observed drift relative to Stage 1. Current SHA-256: 51fb4fa5d62915034c142c4037f139e231986dd50e3bc42dde7d60bdd623bbdc. It was read only, not modified/restored or causally attributed. It is not an asset save target.
  • Both recovery checkpoints remain unchanged and are on G:; they are scoped recovery rather than a complete independent project archive.
  • Saving and reload remain separate unpassed gates. No saved-adoption or persisted-geometry claim is made.

Evidence directory: [local path]

11. Final verdict

READY — MANUAL SAVE REQUIRED

The installed UE source establishes the ordinary File → Save Current Level route independently of the blocked adapter. For the current verified state, its selected set matches exactly the 17 authorized existing Landscape packages, with the clean map excluded and no package deletions. It bypasses the ForgeMCP automatic production-file restoration wrapper without modifying the plugin.

Both recovery checkpoints, original source checksums, current namespace membership, free storage, layer/height/proxy integrity and exact dirty package ownership pass review. No save, adoption repeat, layer creation, sculpt, generation, reload, close, restart, rebuild or restore occurred.

Execution stops at the required human save checkpoint. After the user performs the one manual command, continue with read-only validation before making any persistence claim.
